__models.gap: docs/FORMATS.md §5 — "No @skills-dir plugin exists locally" (161 directories under ~/.claude/skills/, not one contains .claude-plugin/plugin.json)
__models.role: TEST ORACLE for ./skills/ — one true positive, three false-positive traps, one plain-personal negative.

detectionRule.statement: A directory under the personal skills root is an @skills-dir plugin if and only if it contains `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.
detectionRule.source: docs/tasks.md T1.4 ("Detect @skills-dir plugins by their .claude-plugin/plugin.json"); docs/02-architecture.md §4.1 (manifests load only from .claude-plugin/)
detectionRule.antiRule: Do NOT glob `**/plugin.json`. FORMATS.md §0 trap #14: sibling .cursor-plugin/ .codex-plugin/ .kimi-plugin/ manifests make that return ~2x the real count — 16 files for 7 plugins on the reference machine.

expected.why: NEGATIVE — a plain personal skill directory, the shape all 161 reference-machine directories have. Also collides by name with the plugin-contributed synthetic-bravo-skill (see shadowing below).
NEGATIVE — carries .cursor-plugin/plugin.json and no Claude Code manifest. A `**/plugin.json` glob promotes it; the correct rule does not.
NEGATIVE — a well-formed manifest at the directory root instead of inside .claude-plugin/. Claude Code does not load it, so ccatlas must not report it.

counts.__countNote: 6 files are named plugin.json under ./skills/. Exactly ONE is a Claude Code manifest. A detector reporting 6, 5 or 2 plugins has fallen into trap #14; a detector reporting 0 is looking one directory level too shallow.

shadowing.__note: Feeds T1.7. Both records must be emitted, with the precedence winner named — never silently deduplicated.

entries.name: synthetic-bravo-skill
entries.winnerStatus: The personal-vs-plugin skill precedence order is not recorded in docs/FORMATS.md and was not observed. This fixture asserts only that BOTH are reported; it deliberately does not assert which wins.

This is a partial fixture for the §5 gap "A command name colliding across two plugins": it collides personal-vs-plugin, not plugin-vs-plugin.

identityForm.question: What is a @skills-dir plugin's canonical id? Marketplace-sourced plugins are `<plugin>@<marketplace>` (FORMATS.md §1), and the marketplace name appears ONLY in that suffix. A @skills-dir plugin has no marketplace.
identityForm.note: docs/01-prd.md §99 lists `@skills-dir` as an ORIGIN, alongside `marketplace`, `personal`, `project` and `--plugin-dir`. This fixture therefore asserts `origin: "skills-dir"` and leaves the id form to T1.6's normalisation. Whatever T1.6 picks, it must not collide with a real marketplace named `skills-dir`.

distinguishingFromMarketplaceSourced.rule: A marketplace-sourced plugin has an entry in `plugins/installed_plugins.json` and a key in `settings.json → enabledPlugins`, and lives under `plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`. This plugin has NONE of those: it lives under the personal skills root, and is absent from both files.
distinguishingFromMarketplaceSourced.status: DERIVED from FORMATS.md §2 — the two populations are disjoint by location, so the check is 'is its path under plugins/cache/?', not a manifest-content check.
distinguishingFromMarketplaceSourced.consequence: Its enabled state has no home. `enabledPlugins` is the ONLY home of the enabled bit (FORMATS.md §2) and it has no key there. ccatlas must report its state as `enabled (implicit)` or `unknown` — NOT `disabled` — and must not synthesise an enabledPlugins key for it.
